title: Editorial: Generative AI in education
extended_summary:
This editorial introduces a Frontiers Research Topic on generative AI in education and summarizes 11 included papers. The broad question addressed is how generative AI, including ChatGPT and other large language models, is being used across educational contexts and what opportunities and challenges it presents for learning, assessment, and support.

The editorial does not report a single intervention study; instead, it synthesizes the themes of the papers in the special issue. These include AI for feedback generation, adolescent use of generative AI for schoolwork, critical thinking support, ChatGPT for pre-service mathematics teachers’ proof construction, whole-learner modeling, personalized assessment, AI mentors for STEM career exploration, academic integrity, interactive listening task generation, and deception detection in educational AI robots.

One of the summarized studies involved 22 Japanese middle school students interacting with generative AI robots and examining their ability to detect lies; the editorial notes that most students were deceived and that there were no significant differences in learning effectiveness, motivation, or encouragement across conditions. More generally, the editorial concludes that generative AI shows promise for personalized learning, feedback, and engagement, but raises concerns about accuracy, emotional appropriateness, interpretability, ethics, privacy, fairness, and the risk of deceptive or harmful outputs.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial/perspective piece summarizing a research topic rather than reporting a primary empirical study. It does not present a clear analytic methodology or original outcomes on student learning.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct intervention effect is estimated in this paper, so there is no measurable educational impact to classify. The article is useful as a field overview but reports no quantitative impact on learners.

interventions.use_case: Editorial overview of generative AI and chatbots such as ChatGPT used for tutoring, feedback, assessment support, and student assistance in education, including mathematics-related use cases discussed in the research topic.
